title: BRADFORD PROPERTY FLOOD RESILIENCE SCHEME
description:
Undertake PFR surveys with a post-installation effectiveness investigation on 48 properties located within the Shipley and Bingley areas of Bradford District. The properties have been identified as being at a higher risk from flooding. With the exception of one, all other identified properties have received PFR measures previously via claims through the 2015 Defra post-flood recovery grant scheme. 

Due to the scale of the 2015 flood event and the significant number of claims for the grant scheme at the time, details of what PFR was installed and the products subsequent effectiveness during flood events over the following 8 years is limited. 

The aim of the surveys is to provide the City of Bradford Metropolitan District Council (MDC) with an overview of the current condition of the existing PFR measures, any missing protection elements and any issues associated with the products usage, maintenance and storage. This information will help form an evidence base in support of a future potential PFR maintenance or full replacement programme in the area. Bradford MDC also wish to gain an understanding from residents of the impacts of any flooding since the installation of PFR, with the effectiveness and experiences of using the PFR measures during the event.

description:

Full Business Case Development
Full Business Case Determination

The Steeton and Silsden Active Travel Corridor Scheme is a City Region Sustainable Transport Settlement (CRSTS) project being delivered by City of Bradford Metropolitan District Council (the Client). The proposed scheme objectives are outlined below: 
•	Eliminate the key barrier to active travel between Steeton and Silsden by overcoming the severance of the A629 
•	Improve cycling and walking access to facilities, services, education, and employment opportunities, such as Steeton and Silsden Station and Airedale Hospital from Steeton & Silsden town centres 
•	Make active travel a natural and popular choice for local and short distance trips and deliver a 20% uplift in walking and a 50% uplift in cycling between Steeton and Silsden within 5 years of the scheme opening. 
•	Improve the perception of safety for cyclists and pedestrians traveling between Steeton and Silsden 
•	Enhance air quality and contribute to decarbonisation through a mode shift to active travel 
•	Complement future housing growth through the provision of sustainable journey options to/from allocated sites 
•	The project will be funded by the West Yorkshire Combined Authority through the City Region Sustainable Transport Settlements

title: Processing of Co-mingled Dry Mixed Recycling (DMR)
description: The City of Bradford Metropolitan District Council (the Council) is seeking to source a suitably licensed Contractor to deliver the Service which is composed of the keeping, recycling and treating of Comingled DMR. The Council currently collect around 42,000 tonnes of co-mingled DMR at kerbside each year which is then processed at either the Council's and/or Contractors MRF prior to the resulting product being processed for subsequent sale. Currently; glass, cans, plastic. Paper and card are collected in the same kerbside bin. This may change to segregated collections during the contract, subject to the announcement on the "Consistent Collections" policy. The main objective of the contract is to divert waste away from landfill and to improve the Council's National Indicator "NI192" performance. The contract is required to start approximately 19th June 2023 and will run for a fixed period of three years until 31st May 2026 with the option to extend for an additional two-year period. -	To provide initial, continual, and appropriate support and guidance for school staff and leadership in delivering materials to promote resilience to maximise the impact of the program
-	To provide resources and support for parents/carer and significant others to support embedding the methods in family homes using a range of means to narrow inequalities in access
-	Provide assured monitoring of the use of approach and materials and regular reporting to the Bradford District and Craven Health and Care partnership and NHSE

-	Evaluation of the model to describe and demonstrate the impact of the program on prevention and ultimately decreased demand on specialist children and young people mental health services

title: Main Contract Works
description:
Kala Sangam Arts Centre (KSAC) is an intercultural arts venue based in Bradford city centre and is an Arts Council England National Portfolio Organisation. It presents two seasons of diverse performances annually; engages children and adults through a range of classes, workshops and schools' activity; and delivers a year-round programme of artist development and support. 
 
KSAC hosts work not seen on other stages in the North and a range of activity unique to Bradford. The organisation plays a national role in the development of dance and is the only venue in the North prioritising support for South Asian arts.  
 
KSAC is a Grade II Listed building and Bradford's old Post Office. Its redevelopment will be a key capital milestone of Bradford's UK City of Culture delivery in 2025.

KSAC is now seeking a main contractor to undertake a significant remodelling and refurbishment scheme.  The works comprise the following:

•	Internal structural alterations
•	Formation of a new 200 seat theatre space on the ground floor. 
•	New layout for the existing studio theatre. 
•	A welcoming and spacious entrance foyer on the ground floor with direct access from the street through a new entrance, reception area and box office. 
•	Provision of new multi-use spaces with potential for hosting meetings etc. 
•	Provision of new studio spaces 
•	Lift replacement x 2
•	Partial roof replacement 
•	Creation of a new tenant area to accommodate BCB Radio on the ground floor with separate and controlled out of hours access. 

The appointment of a main contractor is being undertaken as a two stage process.  This initial step is for interested parties to submit a Selection Questionnaire, which will be scored on the criteria set out in the Questionnaire.  A maximum of 5 - the highest scoring companies - will then be invited to proceed to the second stage of the procurement and submit a tender.  

The tender stage is effectively the first stage of a two stage traditional works procurement  and will be sought on a 60/40 Price/Quality basis.  The tender will cover the following; -
•	Preliminaries
•	Pre-construction phase fees
•	Contractors overhead, profit and attendances on net costs.
•	Establishing the capabilities of the tendering parties to deliver this project
•	Demonstrating the tendering parties can meet the qualitative, environmental and/or social aspects linked to this project.

Following appointment, the contractor will work with the design team to finalise the design and undertake second stage procurement, tendering individual packages (including CDP) to produce a Contract Sum for the works which will provide KSAC with a complete, fitted out building.

The Employer is not bound to accept the lowest or any Tender.

The contract will be the JCT Standard Building Contract without Quantities 2016 (SBC/XQ 2016) with amendments.

To download the procurement documentation, please visit https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fo/u24loiqa1bvbx0bdn1d6b/h?rlkey=v4zw41qdk2y0192pkxx7ees3y&dl=0

title: Telemedicine Service - Bradford District and Craven Health and Care Partnership
description:
The service will provide on-demand video based clinical consultations which will be available 24/7

The TMS Includes:
-	Initial clinical assessment by an appropriately trained registered practitioner
-	Escalation to other specialist clinical resources (e.g., an appropriately qualified consultant, medical registrar, or specialist nurse) where required
-	Coordination with local clinical resources (district nurses, community teams, ambulance service and the resident's GP) where required
-	24/7 clinical assessment and support for all residents who fall to reduce attendance at ED and acute admission
-	Provision of virtual meeting room to facilitate community service providers and other relevant partners to conduct their MDT meetings
-	Consultant Pharmacist support on prescribing, deprescribing, mentoring/training, medicines safety and research. Input to developing services responsive to local needs and available as an expert resource.
-	Clinical support for safer implementation of Medicines Optimisation
-	Support for the DES Requirements of the Enhanced Health in Care Homes Initiative

The principal mechanism for consultations will be video but voice calls and other forms of communication will be used where necessary. All consultations will be recorded via SystmOne into the patient record and a copy of this will be supplied to the GP. 

Each clinical consultation will entail: 
-	Initial assessment of the person's condition by a registered practitioner 
-	Escalation to a suitably qualified consultant, medical registrar or specialist nurse if required 
-	Administration of a prescription if required 
-	Referral to and/or coordination with the persons GP, district or community nursing team, ambulance service to include any phone calls or video calls required 
-	Provision of advice and guidance to the persons local carers 
-	Clinical supervision of any procedures or other activities undertaken by the local carers at the request of the clinical assessors 
-	Follow-up calls by the TMS team to check on the person's progress 
-	Creation and updating of the electronic patient record to include the TMS clinical consultation and the supply of a copy of that record to the GP. 

If required CH staff will be offered clinical supervision by the TMS to perform basic procedures.
